title: Llm.asm – Pure x86-64 Assembly for LLM Inference and Training

excerpt: Three complete LLM projects written in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly. Zero C, zero C++, zero Rust, zero libc, zero libm, zero runtime dependencies. Assembled directly with nasm and linked with ld. Every math kernel (expf, sincosf, RMSNorm, RoPE, SiLU, Softmax), AVX2+FMA+F16C GEMM/GEMV engine, BPE tokenizer, clone()/futex() thread pool, bare-metal SMP kernel, analytical backward pass, AdamW optimizer, and live Unicode Braille TUI is hand-written x86-64 assembly (17,252 lines total across all three projects). Measured on the same machine (AMD EPYC 7642, 47C online, 256 MiB L3, DDR4, CPU-only -ngl 0), same model (Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0: 613.66 MiB .asmbin v2 FP16-scale vs 604.15 MiB GGUF Q8_0), 34 prompt tokens / 64 generated tokens, 3-run average: (Note: llama.cpp uses batched GEMM for prompt prefill pp34, whereas llm.asm runs token-by-token GEMV. For autoregressive decode tg64, llm.asm (FAST_Q8=1) combines INT8xINT8 AVX2 vpmaddubsw/vpmaddwd, .asmbin v2 FP16 block scales (F16C vcvtph2ps), monotonic next-row prefetch, contiguous head-major KV-cache, and parallel GQA attention — beating llama.cpp by +18%..+36% across 1..40 threads while producing bit-exact deterministic outputs across all thread counts.
